```{r}
# 1. Converter o objeto de survey mantendo a integridade
design_tidy <- as_survey(pnadc_financing)

# 2. Categorizar, ordenar as faixas do MCMV e calcular os percentuais
tabela_mcmv_regiao <- design_tidy %>%
  mutate(
    faixa_mcmv_texto = case_when(
      household_income <= 2850 ~ "Faixa 1",
      household_income > 2850 & household_income <= 4700 ~ "Faixa 2",
      household_income > 4700 & household_income <= 8600 ~ "Faixa 3",
      household_income > 8600 ~ "Acima da Faixa 3",
      TRUE ~ "Ignorado"
    ),
    faixa_mcmv = factor(faixa_mcmv_texto, levels = c(
      "Acima da Faixa 3",
      "Faixa 3",
      "Faixa 2",
      "Faixa 1",
      "Ignorado"
    ))
  ) %>%
  group_by(macroregion, faixa_mcmv) %>%
  summarize(
    domicilios_estimados = survey_total(na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  group_by(macroregion) %>%
  mutate(
    percentual_na_regiao = (domicilios_estimados / sum(domicilios_estimados)) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Construir o gráfico 100% Stacked Column com legenda no canto inferior direito
grafico_mcmv <- ggplot(tabela_mcmv_regiao, aes(x = macroregion, y = percentual_na_regiao, fill = faixa_mcmv)) +
  geom_col() + 
  
  geom_text(
    aes(label = gsub("\\.", ",", sprintf("%.1f%%", percentual_na_regiao))), 
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",                        
    size = 3
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Faixa 1" = "#2066a8", 
      "Faixa 2" = "#3594cc", 
      "Faixa 3" = "#8cc5e3", 
      "Acima da Faixa 3" = "#A0A0A0",
      "Ignorado" = "#E0E0E0"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "População projetada (%)",
    fill = "Faixas de renda (PMCMV)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # Moves legend below the plot area
    legend.position = "right",

    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(grafico_mcmv)

ggsave(
  filename = "../outputs/chart_mcmv.png", 
  plot = grafico_mcmv,
  width = 11,      # Increase this value to stretch the chart area
  height = 5,      # Keep height standard to create a widescreen aspect ratio
  dpi = 300,       # High resolution for publications
  bg = "white"     # Ensures a white background
)
```

```{r}
compute_cv_by_bracket <- function(design_obj, threshold = 8600, region_label = "") {
  
  below <- subset(design_obj, household_income <= threshold)
  above <- subset(design_obj, household_income > threshold)
  
  summarize_segment <- function(seg_design, segment_label) {
    mean_val <- svymean(~household_income, seg_design, na.rm = TRUE)
    var_val  <- svyvar(~household_income, seg_design, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Index by position (1st/only element) instead of by name --
    # svyvar()'s coef() doesn't reliably carry the "household_income"
    # label the way svymean()'s does, especially for svyrep.design.
    mu  <- as.numeric(coef(mean_val))[1]
    sd_ <- sqrt(as.numeric(coef(var_val))[1])
    cv  <- sd_ / mu
    
    n_obs <- nrow(seg_design$variables)
    
    data.frame(
      Regiao  = region_label,
      Faixa   = segment_label,
      N       = n_obs,
      Media   = mu,
      DP      = sd_,
      CV      = cv
    )
  }
  
  rbind(
    summarize_segment(below, paste0("<= R$", format(threshold, big.mark = ".", scientific = FALSE))),
    summarize_segment(above, paste0("> R$", format(threshold, big.mark = ".", scientific = FALSE)))
  )
}

cv_sul     <- compute_cv_by_bracket(pnadc_financing_sul, threshold = 8600, region_label = "Sul")
cv_sudeste <- compute_cv_by_bracket(pnadc_financing_sudeste, threshold = 8600, region_label = "Sudeste")

cv_comparison <- rbind(cv_sul, cv_sudeste)
print(cv_comparison)
```

## Tabelas regionais

```{r}
## =================================================================
## Build a table of Exp(B) (odds ratios), split into sections by
## tenure_condition category, with all variables listed under each
## section -- one block for morador_informal, one for proprietario_formal
## (or whichever non-reference categories the model actually has).
## =================================================================
## NOTE on suffix mapping: VGAM multinomial coefficient names look like
## "age:1", "age:2" -- these numeric suffixes correspond to the model's
## internal linear-predictor order, NOT necessarily the order you'd
## guess from eyeballing level labels. Rather than assume an order, this
## function reads it directly from fitted(model)'s column names (the
## same category names/order already verified via colnames(pred_probs)
## elsewhere in this pipeline), dropping the reference category to get
## the correct suffix -> category mapping.

build_exp_b_table_by_category <- function(model_list, digits = 3) {
  
  # ---- Derive suffix -> category mapping from the FIRST model, then
  #      verify every other model agrees (they should, since all were
  #      fit on the same tenure_condition categories).
  get_category_order <- function(model) {
    fv <- fitted(model)
    colnames(fv)
  }
  
  ref_model <- model_list[[1]]
  all_categories <- get_category_order(ref_model)
  
  for (region in names(model_list)[-1]) {
    this_categories <- get_category_order(model_list[[region]])
    if (!identical(this_categories, all_categories)) {
      warning(sprintf(
        "Category order for '%s' (%s) differs from '%s' (%s) -- check whether all regional models were fit on the same tenure_condition factor levels.",
        region, paste(this_categories, collapse = ", "),
        names(model_list)[1], paste(all_categories, collapse = ", ")
      ))
    }
  }
  
  # The reference category has NO coefficient/suffix of its own -- the
  # remaining categories, in order, correspond to suffix 1, 2, ... in
  # the coefficient names.
  coef_names_ref <- names(coef(ref_model))
  suffixes_used  <- sort(unique(as.integer(sub(".*:([0-9]+)$", "\\1", coef_names_ref))))
  non_ref_categories <- setdiff(all_categories, NA)  # placeholder, replaced below
  
  # Identify the reference category: the one NOT implied by any suffix.
  # Safer approach: VGAM lists non-reference categories in the same
  # order as `all_categories` with the reference one removed -- but
  # since we don't know a priori WHICH is the reference from fitted()
  # alone, infer it from the model's own refLevel if available.
  ref_level_idx <- tryCatch(ref_model@misc$refLevel, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(ref_level_idx)) ref_level_idx <- 1  # VGAM default
  non_ref_categories <- all_categories[-ref_level_idx]
  
  message("Suffix -> category mapping used:")
  for (i in seq_along(non_ref_categories)) {
    message(sprintf("  :%d  ->  %s", i, non_ref_categories[i]))
  }
  message(sprintf("(Reference category: %s)", all_categories[ref_level_idx]))
  
  # ---- Helper: strip the ":N" suffix to get the base variable name
  base_name <- function(x) sub(":[0-9]+$", "", x)
  suffix_num <- function(x) as.integer(sub(".*:([0-9]+)$", "\\1", x))
  
  all_vars_full <- unique(unlist(lapply(model_list, function(m) names(coef(m)))))
  all_base_vars <- unique(base_name(all_vars_full))
  
  build_block <- function(suffix_n, category_label) {
    block <- data.frame(tenure_condition = category_label,
                        Variable = all_base_vars, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    for (region in names(model_list)) {
      model <- model_list[[region]]
      cn    <- names(coef(model))
      exp_b <- exp(coef(model))
      
      keep <- suffix_num(cn) == suffix_n & !is.na(suffix_num(cn))
      sub_names <- base_name(cn[keep])
      sub_vals  <- exp_b[keep]
      
      matched <- sub_vals[match(block$Variable, sub_names)]
      block[[region]] <- round(unname(matched), digits)
    }
    block
  }
  
  blocks <- lapply(seq_along(non_ref_categories), function(i) {
    build_block(i, non_ref_categories[i])
  })
  
  result <- do.call(rbind, blocks)
  rownames(result) <- NULL
  result
}
```

```{r}
model_list <- list(
  "Norte"        = post_lasso_norte,
  "Nordeste"     = post_lasso_nordeste,
  "Sudeste"      = post_lasso_sudeste,
  "Sul"          = post_lasso_sul,
  "Centro-Oeste" = post_lasso_centroeste
)

exp_b_table <- build_exp_b_table_by_category(model_list)

# To get morador_informal's section first, proprietario_formal second
# (or whatever order you want), reorder the tenure_condition factor:
exp_b_table$tenure_condition <- factor(
  exp_b_table$tenure_condition,
  levels = c("morador_informal", "proprietario_formal")
)
exp_b_table <- exp_b_table[order(exp_b_table$tenure_condition), ]

View(exp_b_table)
knitr::kable(exp_b_table, digits = 2)
```

```{r}
# 1. Defina o vetor com os nomes exatos das suas regiões
regions <- c("norte", "nordeste", "sudeste", "sul", "centroeste")

# 2. Extraia os níveis reais da variável dependente para nomear as seções automaticamente[cite: 1]
niveis_estimados <- levels(pnadc$variables$tenure_condition)[-1]

# 3. Criar um data.frame vazio para empilhar os resultados de todas as regiões
all_regions_df <- data.frame()

for (reg in regions) {
  # Chama o objeto do modelo regional da memória dinamicamente (ex: post_lasso_Norte)
  mod_name <- paste0("post_lasso_", reg)
  mod <- get(mod_name)
  mod_sum <- summary(mod)
  
  # Extração estrutural blindada da matriz do modelo svyVGAM[cite: 1]
  if ("coeftable" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
    raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coeftable
  } else if ("coefficients" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
    raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coefficients
  } else if ("coef3" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
    raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coef3
  } else {
    raw_matrix <- as.matrix(mod_sum)
  }
  
  # Cria a tabela temporária extraindo apenas o Estimate_B (Coluna 1)
  temp_df <- data.frame(
    Term = rownames(raw_matrix),
    Estimate_B = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 1]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Calcula o Odds Ratio (Exp(B)) e marca a qual região esses dados pertencem
  temp_df$Exp_B <- exp(temp_df$Estimate_B)
  temp_df$Region <- reg
  
  # Empilha na tabela principal
  all_regions_df <- rbind(all_regions_df, temp_df)
}

# 4. Limpeza dos termos e mapeamento para as categorias de moradia
all_regions_df$Variable <- sub(":.*", "", all_regions_df$Term)
all_regions_df$Eq_Index <- as.numeric(sub(".*:", "", all_regions_df$Term))

# Traduz o índice numérico da equação para o nome real da categoria (ex: "Morador informal")[cite: 1]
all_regions_df$Category <- niveis_estimados[all_regions_df$Eq_Index]

# 5. Pivotar a tabela (Variáveis nas linhas, Regiões nas colunas)
table_wide <- all_regions_df %>%
  select(Category, Variable, Region, Exp_B) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Region,
    values_from = Exp_B
  )

# 6. Gerar a tabela acadêmica com o pacote gt
final_table <- table_wide %>%
  # Agrupa pelas categorias de moradia para criar as seções (Category)
  group_by(Category) %>%
  gt() %>%
  # Formata os números de todas as colunas regionais para 3 casas decimais
  fmt_number(
    columns = all_of(regions),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**TABLE 5**"),
    subtitle = "Odds Ratios (Exp(B)) by Region and Tenure Choice"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    row_group.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.background.color = "#f0f0f0",
    table.border.top.color = "black",
    table.border.bottom.color = "black",
    table_body.hlines.color = "lightgray"
  )

# Visualizar a tabela
final_table
```
